root.lessons: Investigated black-box LLM confidence elicitation across calibration & failure prediction. (1) Recalled the 3-axis design space (prompting x sampling x aggregation) and the two distinct metrics ECE vs AUROC. (2) Real GPT-5.5 stand-in experiment (N=16): verbalized confidences cluster strongly at round numbers (13/16 multiples of 5) and are miscalibrated (ECE=0.234) — but a STRONG stand-in was UNDER-confident, the opposite of the paper's overconfident GPT-3.5, confirming miscalibration SIGN is model-dependent while clustering is universal. (3) Sampling+consistency is the literature's main failure-prediction lever, but a strong stand-in makes too few errors to show its edge, and a Monte-Carlo sim cannot adjudicate (its winner is assumption-driven) — verifying the effect needs the real weaker models/GPU we lack. (4) Calibration and failure prediction are distinct axes: even with poor ECE, verbalized confidence still localized all errors to its low-confidence slice (good relative ranking). (5) White-box internals methods (logits/P(True)/probes) and full cross-model reproduction are BLOCKED (no GPU/API) and recorded honestly as needs_review.

q1-search.current_hypothesis: Recall the black-box confidence elicitation framework and evaluation metrics from the literature (Xiong et al. ICLR 2024 'Can LLMs Express Their Uncertainty?').
q1-search.key_evidence: Recalled: the framework factorizes black-box elicitation into 3 components. (1) PROMPTING strategy: Vanilla/verbalized ('give answer and confidence 0-100'), Chain-of-Thought, Self-Probing ('how likely is your answer correct?'), Multi-Step (confidence per reasoning step), Top-K (give K guesses each with prob). (2) SAMPLING strategy: Self-Random (multiple samples at temperature>0), Prompt-paraphrasing, Misleading hints. (3) AGGREGATION: Consistency (fraction agreeing with the majority/given answer), Avg-Conf (mean verbalized conf over samples), Pair-Rank. Evaluation: CALIBRATION via ECE (Expected Calibration Error) and reliability diagrams; FAILURE PREDICTION via AUROC/AUPRC of confidence separating correct vs wrong answers. Datasets: GSM8K/SVAMP (math), CSQA/StrategyQA/Sports (commonsense), Law/Ethics/Business (professional). Models: GPT-3.5-turbo, GPT-4, Llama-2, Vicuna.

q1-read.current_hypothesis: What does the literature report about verbalized-confidence calibration?
q1-read.key_evidence: Key reported findings recalled: (a) LLMs are systematically OVERCONFIDENT when verbalizing confidence — verbalized numbers (often 80-100%) exceed actual accuracy, giving high ECE (e.g., GPT-3.5 vanilla ECE ~0.2-0.4 on several sets). (b) Verbalized confidences CLUSTER at round numbers (multiples of 5/10) and at the high end, limiting resolution. (c) Failure prediction (AUROC) from raw verbalized confidence is often near 0.5-0.7 — weak separation of right vs wrong. (d) Sampling+CONSISTENCY (self-consistency style agreement) generally improves AUROC/failure prediction more than calibration. (e) Hybrid 'Top-K + Avg-Conf + consistency' (their 'COT+Agg') is best overall. (f) Stronger models (GPT-4) are better calibrated than GPT-3.5; harder datasets degrade both.
q1-read.main_risk: Exact numbers vary by dataset/model; treating these as qualitative claims to test, not exact reproduction targets.
q1-read.next_action: Form hypothesis H1 (verbalized confidence overconfident + round-number clustering) and test on a small stand-in set.

AUROC needs many error cases to be meaningful.

q2-sim.current_hypothesis: Does a Monte-Carlo simulation adjudicate consistency vs verbalized confidence?
q2-sim.key_evidence: Simulation (N=2000, k=10 samples, illustrative ONLY): I coupled verbalized confidence to true correctness prob p (monotonic + round-number snapping + noise) and consistency to k Bernoulli(p) draws. (e) Verbalized confidence remains overconfident and round-number-clustered across models; black-box methods narrow but do not close the gap to white-box.
